transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I feel drained all the time, like I don’t have the energy to get through my workday or even enjoy fishing on the weekends. It's just gotten to the point where I'm struggling to do much of anything, and a friend suggested I should come get checked out.
Have you felt this way for most of the last two years, or is this a new change that has only been happening for a few weeks or months?

It hasn't been two years, but these cycles of highs and lows have been going on off and on for about a year now. This current low, drained feeling has actually been hanging over me for most of the past eleven months, only letting up briefly during those times when I get those revved-up bursts of energy.
During those 'revved-up' bursts of energy, have you ever felt so energized or irritable that it significantly disrupted your ability to work or socialize, or required hospitalization?

During those high times, I felt really energetic, stayed up late working on tech projects, and spent too much money on gear, but it never led to hospitalization or majorly disrupted my life. The real problems, like getting written up at work and pulling away from friends, actually happen when I crash into these low, drained periods.
During the past year, have there been any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt completely symptom-free and back to your normal self?

No, I haven't had any breaks that lasted that long over the past year. I've felt stuck in this low mood for most of the past eleven months, and the only breaks I get are those brief, revved-up bursts rather than actually feeling back to my normal, stable self.

This clinical picture of chronic, fluctuating mood symptoms that do not meet the full criteria for major depressive or manic episodes is most consistent with F34.0. F31.8 is less likely as the symptoms are primarily characterized by a chronic, sub-threshold course rather than distinct, severe bipolar cycles.
